title: Editing content: plain files or Sveltia CMS
author: subimpact network
excerpt: All Kaze content is JSON in your repo. Edit it directly, or set up the optional Sveltia CMS editor for people who prefer a browser interface.
body:
Everything Kaze builds comes from files in `content/`. The generator never talks to a database or an API.

## Editing files directly

Open the JSON files in any editor, change them, and run the build:

```bash
python3 build.py
```

While working locally, `python3 dev.py` rebuilds on every change and serves the site at `http://localhost:8000`. Refresh the browser to see changes.

Article bodies are a Markdown string inside the JSON file. Use `\n` for line breaks inside the JSON string.

## Using Sveltia CMS (optional)

The `admin/` folder contains a [Sveltia CMS](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms) setup. Sveltia is an open-source, Git-based editor that runs in the browser and commits changes to your repository. It reads `admin/config.yml`, which follows the Decap CMS configuration format.

It does not work out of the box. You need to:

1. Set `repo` in `admin/config.yml` to your GitHub repository.
2. Provide GitHub authentication. GitHub OAuth needs a small server-side step, usually a Cloudflare Worker such as the Sveltia CMS Authenticator, set as `base_url` in the config.
3. Deploy the site so `/admin/` is reachable.

If you do not need a browser editor, delete the `admin/` folder. The build does not depend on it.

## Why files

Your content stays in Git, with full history, and you can move it to another generator later. The JSON fields are documented by example in the files in `content/`.
